questions.q: In the content engine, how is the work divided between you and AI?
options: You supply the thinking once, AI reshapes it, and you edit before publishing
AI comes up with the ideas, and you approve the monthly calendar
AI writes and publishes everything, and you review the results monthly
You write every piece yourself, and AI only schedules the posts
questions.explain: The lesson defines the content engine as you supplying the thinking once, AI handling the reshaping into many formats, and a person editing before anything goes out.

questions.q: A kitchen remodeler asks AI to 'write a blog post about kitchen renovations' and gets a generic article. What fix does the lesson recommend?
options: Ask for a longer article with more keywords and subheadings
Generate ten versions and publish whichever performs best
Feed it customer questions, his opinions and anonymized job stories
Ask the AI to add statistics so the article stands out
questions.explain: The lesson says AI-only content has no point of view or experience, and the fix is feeding the engine raw material only you have: customer questions, your opinions and anonymized stories from your work.

questions.q: A pet-supply store owner's AI-drafted newsletter contains an [ADD EXAMPLE] marker and a statistic she doesn't recognize. What should happen before it goes out?
options: Send it as is, since the pillar prompt already used the voice guide
Resolve the marker and remove or verify the unfamiliar statistic
Delete the marker but keep the statistic, since it adds credibility
Ask the AI whether the statistic is accurate and trust its answer
questions.explain: The human edit pass requires every fact, number and claim to be true and yours, and every [ADD EXAMPLE] and [CHECK] marker to be resolved before anything is published.
